text:
maria: Heads-up — spotted an unexpected line on the Feb invoice: "GPUs: Preemptible surcharge - asia-east2" for $12,340. We have no active workloads in asia-east2. Can infra confirm?

ajay: Hmm. We don't deploy there intentionally. Could be a fallback from burst routing or a mistaken reservation. Tagging @kevin for oncall. :eyes:

kevin: Looking now. Checking recent autoscale/placement logs and routing policies. If any batch jobs spilled into asia-east2 they would've been transient. Pasting the invoice snippet I pulled: ```
LineItem: GPUs - Preemptible surcharge
SKU: GPU-PREEM-SUR+asia-east2
Quantity: 72 GPU-hours
Charge: $12,340.00
Account: prod-inference-us-central
```

ops-bot: Support case created: CASE-987654 (gcp). Assigned to billing agent.

sasha: I opened a billing audit earlier because we saw a small region-price delta; could be related. Also saw an unexpected rate change on the provider side last week: provider announced temporary pricing override for asia-east2 on 2026-02-11. I'll paste the provider notice: ```
[Provider Notice] 2026-02-11: Temporary surcharge for preemptible GPUs in asia-east2 due to capacity constraints. Effective immediately. Estimated impact: variable.```

gcp-support: Hi team, we've attached CASE-987654 to your account. Preliminary review shows two things: (1) an automated fallback placed preemptible workloads into asia-east2 when your preferred zones exhausted capacity, and (2) an internal rate override was applied that added a surcharge line. We're validating whether the surcharge was applied at time of allocation versus post-usage billing. We will reply with a credit decision within 3 business days.

maria: Thanks. For bookkeeping we need the full breakdown (which project/labels caused the placement). The invoice shows account prod-inference-us-central which is weird. Can infra confirm which cost-center those instances are tagged with?

ajay: Pulling placement logs now. Quick finding: on 2026-02-10 23:41 UTC we had a burst of internal eval jobs (job-id eval-3307) that hit quota in us-central so the placement policy allowed region fallback. The cluster autoscaler launched 72 preemptible GPUs in asia-east2 for ~1.2 hours. Tags: project=infra-evals, cost-center=ml-research. I can share the placement events if helpful.

kevin: That matches. We have two followups: (A) avoid cross-region fallbacks for billing-sensitive jobs (add policy to block asia-east2 fallback), (B) add an invoice-alert rule (threshold + unusual-region) to finance. If GCP grants credit we should still update routings. :thumbsup:

sasha: Agree. Also recommend reserving a small burst buffer in primary regions (reserved capacity commit) so critical evals don't spill. That will likely be cheaper than one-off surcharges. I'll work with finance to cost the commit vs expected surcharge recurrence.

gcp-support: Update: we submitted for a full or partial credit; initial response indicates a potential full credit for the surcharge because these were fallback allocations under capacity pressure. Will confirm.

maria: Great. Please flag me when credit posts. Finance action items: (1) wait on credit, (2) tag cost-center for chargeback, (3) policy to prevent region fallback for prod-eval jobs. Ops: can you add the alert rule and a preemptive reserved-commit estimate?

ajay: On it. I'll add a placement policy PR to block asia-east2 fallback for any job with tag billing-sensitive=true and open a follow-up ticket for reserved commit estimates. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/placement/pull/411

kevin: Closing loop for now. I've added a short-term monitor and will escalate if more unexpected regions show up. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
